source_caption:
To perfectly capture the deeply sadistic, wildly unpredictable cruelty of the boy king, Jack Gleeson drew heavy inspiration from Joaquin Phoenix’s fiercely arrogant performance as the young emperor Commodus in Gladiator. He played the role of Joffrey so incredibly convincingly that author George R.R. Martin famously sent the young actor a personal letter stating: “Congratulations on your marvelous performance, everyone hates you!” Despite portraying one of the most viscerally despised villains in television history, Gleeson is universally described by his co-stars as one of the warmest, most profoundly polite actors on set, frequently apologizing to his castmates immediately after filming his character’s horrific scenes. By leaning so entirely into absolute malice while remaining deeply grounded behind the camera, Gleeson masterfully proves that the most terrifying on-screen monsters are often played by the absolute kindest people.
⠀
Game of Thrones (2011–2019), created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss, starring Emilia Clarke, Peter Dinklage, Kit Harington. In the fiercely brutal, heavily volatile mythical land of Westeros, several profoundly ambitious noble families wage a wildly bloody, deeply devastating war for absolute control of the Iron Throne, all while an ancient, completely terrifying supernatural threat slowly awakens in the frozen north.

source_details.synopsis: Game of Thrones is an American fantasy drama television series created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss for HBO. It is the first adaptation of A Song of Ice and Fire, a series of high fantasy novels by George R. R. Martin, and the first in what would become the Game of Thrones franchise. The show premiered on HBO in the United States on April 17, 2011, and concluded on May 19, 2019, with 73 episodes broadcast over eight seasons. Set on the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos, Game of Thrones has a large ensemble cast and follows several story arcs throughout the course of the show.
